subject: Air-gapped delivery attestation, handover window, and recovery plan
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Air-gapped delivery attestation, handover window, and recovery plan

Jordan —

Following our call yesterday, attaching a first-pass package and an operational proposal for the offline artifact handover and update path you asked for. High level: we intend to deliver a signed bundle that contains the runtime images, model weights, and a small attestation manifest. The transfer will happen on a scheduled physical media handoff to your SOC team. We want to confirm the acceptance checks you need and the emergency recovery path if any artifacts fail validation during install.

Key items attached:
- artifact-manifest-v1.json (SHA256 checksums + provenance fields)
- offline-transfer-checklist.xlsx (step-by-step handoff and acceptance matrix)
- signing-instructions.pdf (how we sign, verification steps, key IDs)

Proposed handover window: Thu 2026-10-07 10:00–13:00 PDT (we can shift). Proposed participants from Redwood on-site: me + Marissa (release engineer).

Acceptance checks we plan to run on your side (suggested):
1) Verify the signature(s) using our public key thumbprint (included in signing-instructions).
2) Validate SHA256 checksums against manifest.
3) Run offline artifact verification tool (we can provide a Docker image or a single static binary).
4) Install to a sealed staging host and run smoke tests (the checklist has the tests).

Recovery / rollback plan (summary):
- If verification fails: media sealed and quarantined; Redwood will provide a new signed bundle after root cause.
- If install fails post-verify: revert to previous snapshot; the offline rollback bundle is included in the package.

Questions for you before we lock schedule:
- Do you require HSM-based key exchange on-site (we currently sign in our KMS and provide public keys, but can coordinate an HSM-to-HSM transfer)?
- Any additional regulatory evidence you need during handoff (e.g., chain-of-custody forms, notarized receipts)?
- Is the suggested acceptance checklist sufficient or do you want to bake in extra crypto validation steps?

Next steps: if you agree to the window we'll send the transfer manifest and a DocuSign acceptance form for your SOC lead to sign before physical handoff.

—
Alex Martinez
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0129

Attachments: artifact-manifest-v1.json, offline-transfer-checklist.xlsx, signing-instructions.pdf

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-fin.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@acme-fin.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 14:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Air-gapped delivery attestation, handover window, and recovery plan

Alex, thanks for the packet — this is helpful. A few quick items from our side: 

1) We will want chain-of-custody paperwork and a signed receipt from the courier. Notarization not required but helpful for audit.
2) HSM: our policy prefers HSM-backed key exchange for initial trust establishment. Can Redwood facilitate a temporary wrapping key that we unwrap into our HSM?
3) The acceptance checklist looks good, but add a requirement that the manifest includes the build-id and full commit SHA for the model artifact (we need immutable linkage to your model repo).

Operationally we can make the 10:00–13:00 PDT window work on Thu 2026-10-07. I will assign Luis from our SOC team to be on-hand for the handoff; copy his contact: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@acme-fin.com>.

One more ask: can you include the offline verification binary as a hashed, signed binary (not a container) for our air-gapped hosts? Containers are harder to run in our sealed environment.

Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Director, Infrastructure Security
Acme Financial
jordan.ellis@acme-fin.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-fin.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped delivery attestation, handover window, and recovery plan

Jordan —
Quick notes from engineering/security:

- HSM flow: we can support an ephemeral wrapping key workflow. Redwood signs artifacts in our KMS; for the handoff we can provision a wrapping key that you unwrap in your HSM and use to verify a short-lived attestation certificate. We'll include the sequence and TTP in signing-instructions.pdf.

- Offline binary: we'll produce a statically linked verifier (linux x86_64) and a separate Mac artifact if needed. Both will be signed and checksummed in the manifest. We will not send a container by default.

- Build provenance: we'll add build-id and commit SHA to every model artifact and to the top-level manifest. We'll also include a minimal SBOM for each binary (format: SPDX-lite JSON).

- Emergency patch path: for critical fixes after handoff we recommend a sealed-second-bundle approach — we stage a second signed package that remains sealed and is only released via mutually-authenticated courier with a signed release form. This reduces the need for live network egress.

I'll coordinate the binaries and updated manifest; target to send v1.1 of the manifest + verifier by Tue 2026-09-21 EOD PST.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@acme-fin.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped delivery attestation, handover window, and recovery plan

Jordan/Luis —

Thanks — good alignment. Summary of confirmed items and action owners: 

- Verified window: Thu 2026-10-07 10:00–13:00 PDT (Alex/Marissa on-site from Redwood; Luis from Acme SOC to receive).
- Signing/keys: Redwood to provide ephemeral wrapping key flow and public verification cert; Rishi to deliver updated signing-instructions and v1.1 manifest by 2026-09-21 EOD PST.
- Artifact contents: runtime images, model weights, rollback bundle, offline verifier binary (statically linked) + SPDX-lite SBOM entries.
- Acceptance checks: signature verification, SHA256 checksum, build-id/commit SHA match, staged install and smoke tests.
- Paperwork: Redwood to prepare chain-of-custody receipt PDF and DocuSign transfer acceptance (link sent once you confirm signatory).

Open items:
- Luis, please confirm the on-site person who will sign the DocuSign form and whether you need Redwood to bring printed hardcopies.
- Jordan, confirm whether you want the sealed-second-bundle process documented as part of the initial transfer packet (we recommend yes for high-risk customers).

I'll circulate the DocuSign link and the final v1.1 manifest once Rishi uploads it this afternoon. Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll keep the acceptance checklist deliberately short to make the handoff smooth for your SOC.

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: chain-of-custody-receipt-template.pdf (will be sent with DocuSign), v1.1-manifest (pending upload)
